title: Assessment of the Equivalent Level of Safety Requirements for Small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
relevance: The thesis documents actual manual landing tests with Great Planes Giant BigStik aircraft. It identifies the 2010 electric test aircraft as an 80-inch, nominal 13–15 lb Giant BigStik and documents a separate 2013 campaign with newly built electric GBS#10 and GBS#11 aircraft. The 2013 results include per-landing touchdown location and centerline-deviation measurements for RC, fixed-view FPV, and VR control modes.
limitations: This is pilot/control and landing-performance evidence, not an instrumented flight-dynamics identification or model-validation study. The 2010 and 2013 aircraft were not the same physical airframe; the original 2010 model was lost in 2011. The 2013 table contains 12 morning trials, including two rookie-VR attempts recorded as did-not-complete, and four afternoon demonstration runs under worsening weather. No raw telemetry or video files are attached to the thesis.

title: Aircraft Manoeuvring for Sensor Aiming
relevance: This thesis presents a distinct 2017 instrumented flight campaign on a Great Planes Giant Big Stik UAV. A 25 September 2017 manual open-loop flight used approximately 400 m circuits at 100 m altitude, steady throttle near 25 m/s, and oscillatory aileron, elevator, and rudder inputs to collect identification and validation data. The physical test configuration is specified as electric, 2 m span by 1.4 m length, and approximately 14 kg maximum takeoff weight including 4.5 kg additional payload capacity (the thesis does not report the test-flight mass); it used a 2700 W motor, Pixhawk autopilot, GPS/compass, 915 MHz telemetry, 2.4 GHz RC input, and an independently logging ADIS16488 IMU. The thesis reports fitted rotational/lift models and later attitude-controller and path-following flight demonstrations.
limitations: The identified model is fit for a fixed forward speed of 25 m/s and uses selected conventional manoeuvres, not a broad aerobatic envelope. The thesis presents plotted flight traces, fit statistics, and path-error tables but the public repository record contains no separate raw-log bundle. Its electric setup differs from the piston-powered Giant Big Stik configuration documented in the already-held Cereceda thesis; physical-airframe identity between these campaigns is not established.

title: Validating Uncertain Aircraft Simulation Models Using Flight Test Data
relevance: Uses a modified University of Minnesota Ultra Stick 25e flight-test platform (1.5 kg, 1.27 m span, 17 m/s cruise) to evaluate simulation-model uncertainty against repeated closed-loop flight responses. The study compares flight-test roll-step histories with 1,000 Monte Carlo model runs. limitations: This is closed-loop simulation-model validation, not a new aerodynamic coefficient-identification study. The 5-degree disturbance used to represent turbulence in the uncertainty model is synthetic; atmospheric turbulence in the flight records was not a controlled input. Results are plotted rather than supplied as raw logs and are specific to the cited 25e configuration and controller.
